paragraphs: He is mentioned in Niddah 6b; but in Menachot, but in Menachot 76a the reading is R. M. bar Rav Kisna.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The words “but in Menachot” occur twice in the supplied text. The abbreviation ר״מ remains unexpanded. The William Davidson digital text of Menachot 76a writes Rav Tuvi bar Kisna, and Niddah 6b writes Rav Tuvi bar Rav Ketina, supporting a possible reading ר״ט for ר״מ without changing the supplied Hebrew.

The actual Davidson Niddah 6b and Menachot 76a paragraphs have Rav Tuvi bar Rav Ketina and Rav Tuvi bar Kisna respectively. The supplied repeated words are restored literally in the new body, while R. M. stays unexpanded. The existing mixed note remains verbatim; its possible ר״ט reading remains a conjecture, not Hebrew repair or a proven correction history.
